system_description.narrative_title: Intersecting wars, markets and AI reshape a fragile global order
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is being pulled simultaneously by kinetic conflicts, a volatile financial cycle and a disruptive technological wave. Regional wars (Iran, Russia‑Ukraine) and energy geopolitics (Hormuz, Venezuela) are driving commodity shocks that amplify inflation and force central banks into a collision course with markets; at the same time, an AI boom and public backlash are reordering firms, jobs and regulatory debates. These processes interconnect and propagate through supply chains, capital markets and alliance politics, producing cascading risks and realignments rather than stable equilibria.
system_description.scope: nation-states and coalitions, military operations, energy and commodity flows, global financial markets and central banks, major technology firms and AI ecosystems, supply chains, multinational contracts and international organisations
system_description.super_system: the globalized international political-economic system (contemporary cross-border trade, finance, security and tech interdependence)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial-monetary subsystem (bond markets, central banks, Treasury policy)
Technology & information subsystem (AI, Big Tech, cyber and regulation)
Energy & commodities subsystem (oil, shipping, strategic reserves and pipelines)
Regional security subsystem (Middle East conflict dynamics; Eurasian war and NATO-Europe security)

variables.name: U.S.–Iran Gulf conflict
variables.description: The United States and Iran are engaged in an escalating exchange of strikes and naval actions centered on the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting shipping and energy flows and entrenching a protracted regional warfront.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and European gray‑zone attacks
variables.description: Russia's sustained offensive against Ukraine, including intensified drone and sabotage operations beyond the front line, is inflicting heavy damage, prompting stepped-up Ukrainian appeals for Western support and testing NATO deterrence and cohesion.

variables.name: Global monetary divergence and bond‑market stress
variables.description: A global surge in long‑term yields driven by divergent central‑bank stances (notably a hawkish U.S. Fed and shifts in other major policy regimes) is raising borrowing costs, straining sovereign finances and forcing new coordination choices among major economies.

variables.name: Reconfiguration of oil supply and strategic energy leverage
variables.description: Major powers and external actors are rewriting energy ties—through strategic deals, asset claims and alternative payment arrangements (for example involving Venezuela and other producers)—reshaping export routes, investment flows and pressures toward de‑dollarisation.

variables.name: AI and strategic tech competition
variables.description: An accelerating global race in AI, semiconductors and platform power — led by U.S. tech firms, Chinese challengers and contested by Western regulators — is driving massive private investment, regulatory backlashes and new systemic cyber/financial risks that reorder industrial leadership.
